Write A, B, C for the angles of triangle ABC and R = OA = OB = OC for its circumradius.

Plan: it suffices to show that AH = 2R·cos A and MaO = R·cos A.

1. OB = OC and MaB = MaC, so OMa is the perpendicular bisector of BC; hence OMa ⟂ BC. (1)

2. Extended law of sines in △CAB, so AB = 2R·sin C. (2)

3. We show that AH = 2R·cos A:

AH = AB·sin∠HBA / sin∠BHA    [law of sines in △BHA]
   = AB·cos A / sin∠BHA    [∠ABH = 90° − A; BH ⟂ AC]
   = AB·cos A / sin C    [C = 180° − ∠AHB; AH ⟂ BC]
   = 2R·cos A    [by (2)] (3)

4. We show that MaO = R·cos A:

MaO = R·sin∠MaBO    [law of sines in △BMaO; ∠OMaB = 90° (OMa ⟂ BC, by (1))]
    = R·cos A    [∠OBMa = 90° − A; central angle ∠BOC = 2∠BAC; OB = OC] (4)

5. AH = 2R·cos A, by (3) and MaO = R·cos A, by (4), so AH : MaO = 2, as required. ∎
